However, no matter how complex the AM modulator or demodulator circuit, they all operate the same way. Once you learn the principles of a simple circuit, the more complex circuits will be easier to understand.
The AM circuits used to modulate and demodulate range from the basic (using diodes) to the complex (using transistors).
Modulation and demodulation circuits are no more difficult to learn than other circuits.
Amplification, filtering, and reshaping circuits should already be familiar to you. Multiplexing and demultiplexing circuits are taught later.
Remember, modulation and demodulation are just one aspect of signal processing.
In this lesson you are taught the circuits that are used in AM to modulate and demodulate.
